findings.title: Double-count skip also drops building-side offsets: Entad_SerenityFocus (MeditationFocusStrength) now does nothing
findings.detail: StatPart_Entad.cs:19 sets offsetsViaWearer = IsWearerStat(parentStat) && !(req.Thing is Pawn). IsWearerStat counts the 'Meditation' category as a wearer category (EntadTraitDef.cs:506-513), and MeditationFocusStrength is category Meditation (Core Stats_Basics_Special.xml). It is a stat of the focus object itself, though. The Furniture trait Entad_SerenityFocus (Defs/EntadBuildings.xml:73) offsets it, and the wearer path (the StatOffsetFromGear postfix) never reaches a building, so the rolled +0.1..0.3 no longer applies anywhere. ExplanationPart (StatPart_Entad.cs:54-56) has no matching skip, so the building's psyfocus explanation still shows the +X the value lacks. Fix at line 19: also require the thing to be equippable, e.g. `&& (req.Thing.def.IsApparel || req.Thing.def.equipmentType != EquipmentType.None)`, so only gear defers to the wearer path.

findings.title: Hidden entad offsets show on the gear's own info card through StatOffsetFromGear
findings.detail: ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats shows StatOffsetFromGear(req.Thing, stat) as the value and 'Final value' of each EquippedStatOffsets entry. Patch_StatOffsetFromGear adds the full entad total there, hidden part included. StatPart_Entad.ExplanationPart hides unrevealed traits in the breakdown, but the number gives the effect away. This happens whenever the item's def has its own equippedStatOffsets entry for a stat a hidden trait also offsets. The postfix can't subtract the hidden part because it also feeds the real pawn value (StatWorker.cs:214). Add a postfix on ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats that rewrites that entry's value as total minus hiddenPart, as InfoTextLineFromGear already does.

findings.title: Hidden stat factors on wearer stats are not part of hiddenPart, so the rebuilt gear line can still reveal them
findings.detail: CompEntad.WearerOffset (CompEntad.cs:178-200) only adds up statOffsets into the hidden part. StatPart_Entad still multiplies the gear's vanilla equipped offset by statFactors inside StatOffsetFromGear (StatPart_Entad.cs:27-28), revealed or not. The InfoTextLineFromGear line, which subtracts only hiddenPart, therefore shows a hidden factor's effect. This is narrow: wearer-stat factors are only allowed where the item's statBases list the stat (EntadTraitDef.cs:448).

findings.title: AddTrait/RemoveTrait on a held item do not clear the holder's stat caches
findings.detail: TraitsChanged (CompEntad.cs:271-280) drops wearerOffsets but calls ClearStatCaches only when MaxHitPoints rescales (RescaleHitPoints). Pawn stats read with a cacheStaleAfterTicks window can keep the old wearer offset for a short while after a trait is added to equipped gear. RevealedChanged does clear them. Opinion on how much it matters: it is cosmetic and short-lived.

findings.title: GearAffectsStat is per def, so a hidden-only sibling of the same def still gets a gear line
findings.detail: PawnHasVisibleEntadOffset returns true if any held item of gearDef has a visible offset. The explanation loop at StatWorker.cs:487 then prints a line for every item of that def, so a hidden-only sibling shows vanilla + 0, the '+0.00' symptom this work fixes. Rare given apparel layers and a single primary weapon.

findings.title: Explanation lines no longer add up to the pawn's final value while a trait is hidden
findings.detail: The rebuilt gear line leaves out hiddenPart, but GetValueUnfinalized adds the full StatOffsetFromGear (hidden included) to the pawn's value. This is intended but visible to players comparing the breakdown with the total.

findings.title: InfoTextLineFromGear postfix replaces __result whole
findings.detail: When hiddenPart is non-zero the postfix rebuilds the string from scratch, so an earlier postfix from another mod that edited the line would be lost. None of the 14 scanned trees patches this method, so there's no precedent and no conflict today.
